title: Efficient Piecewise-Linear Embeddings for Deep Tabular Regression by Guided Breakpoint Allocation

problem.claim: Deep tabular regression networks must model irregular and non-smooth relationships between numerical features and continuous targets.

gap.claim: Embedding performance is sensitive to parameter choices, while the irregularity of tabular data makes effective end-to-end gradient-based parameter discovery difficult.

contributions.claim: Better breakpoint selection for piecewise-linear embeddings can yield substantial gains.
GGPL embeddings use GBDTs as a data-driven prior for breakpoint placement.
GGPL reparameterizes breakpoints for numerical stability and uses stochastic breakpoint deactivation during gradient-based fine-tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On 28 regression datasets, adding GGPL to a range of state-of-the-art deep tabular models produces consistent, significant gains.
GGPL introduces no inference overhead because it is applied only during training.
In controlled MLP experiments, GGPL uses an average of 0.4 times as many breakpoints as prior piecewise-linear embeddings while achieving higher accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular prediction includes important regression applications, and deep tabular models need to represent irregular relationships.
Existing numerical embeddings are sensitive to parameter settings, and gradient-based training may not discover effective settings.
The paper proposes GGPL, combining GBDT-guided breakpoint placement with stable reparameterization and stochastic deactivation.
The authors report improvements across 28 datasets, no inference overhead, and higher accuracy with fewer breakpoints in controlled MLP experiments.
The authors characterize GGPL as an effective numerical embedding for deep tabular regression.

source_observation.claim: Data-driven breakpoint placement is presented as a source of gains for piecewise-linear embeddings.

interpretation.claim: Embedding parameter allocation may be as important as selecting the embedding family.

application.claim: For deep tabular regression, use model-informed priors to initialize or guide numerical embedding parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported regression setting.

unknowns: The 28 datasets, compared models, metrics, and statistical procedures are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe the GBDT configuration or breakpoint optimization details.
The magnitude and variability of the reported improvements are unspecified.
